'''The Power of One''' is one of the ending themes for the English [[dub]] of [[M02|the movie of the same name]]. It is available on the {{pkmn|movie}}'s [[Pokémon the Movie 2000 (soundtrack)|soundtrack]] and is sung by {{wp|Donna Summer}}.

==Remixes==
Several remixes of the song were created and published on {{single|The Power of One|CD and vinyl}}:

* '''Jonathan Peters Club Mix'''
* '''Jonathan Peters Drum-A-Pella'''
* '''Jonathan Peters Radio Mix'''
* '''Jonathan Peters Sound Factory Club Mix'''
* '''Jonathan Peters Sound Factory Dub Mix'''
* '''Tommy Musto Gel Dub'''
* '''Tommy Musto Vocal Mix'''
* '''Musto Beats'''

==Trivia==
*The first stanza of this song was frequently [[List of references to Pokémon in popular culture|quoted]] by Republican Presidential hopeful {{wp|Herman Cain}} in his 2012 campaign, attributing it to "a poet", and referring it as the "closing song to the {{wp|2000 Summer Olympics|2000 Olympics}}".<ref name="Amira, Dan (August 12, 2011)">http://nymag.com/daily/intel/2011/08/did_herman_cain_know_he_was_qu.html</ref> In his concession speech, he stated "I believe these words came from the [[M02|Pokémon movie]]."<ref name="Nelson 1978: 329">http://marquee.blogs.cnn.com/2011/12/05/herman-cain-quotes-pokemon-on-his-way-out/</ref>
* This song is one of the only two Pokémon songs in the world to be released as a {{wp|gramophone record}}, in the form of a [[The Power of One (single)|12" vinyl single and a 2LP maxi single]]. The other is [[Don't Say You Love Me]].
* This song was produced by popular music producer {{wp|David Foster}}, who worked with many famous artists such as {{wp|Michael Jackson}}, {{wp|Madonna}}, {{wp|Beyoncé Knowles}}, and {{wp|Barbra Streisand}}.
** Foster and Summer had previously collaborated in 1996 on the song "{{wp|Whenever There Is Love|Whenever There Is Love}}", the theme to the {{wp|Sylvester Stallone}} film {{wp|Daylight (1996 film)|Daylight}}.
